big_repo: Big Big Big Repository I normally like to clone some repositories to explore them at home, offline, but sometimes, some repos are bigger than I could ever Imagine. https://github.com/mthcht/awesome-lists have about 25GB :o Hopefully this repo is full of details that I will find them useful. Metadata: after removing metadata, 900MB is the real size What 25GB means for a clone A clone is not a copy of the files you see on the web page. It is a copy of the entire history, every version of every file, and every message that describes why the change happened. When a repository collects lists of links, the lists change constantly, and each change leaves a version behind. Twenty thousand small edits produce twenty thousand snapshots of the same text. That is where the size comes from, and it is also why the number felt absurd to me at first. The content I wanted was a few hundred pages of plain text. The container around it was twenty five gigabytes. The metadata is the weight Remove the history and the same repository fits in less than a gigabyte. This is the same lesson I keep finding everywhere: the useful part is small, the bookkeeping around it is enormous. File systems do the same thing, mail servers do the same thing, and any folder with a thousand small files will spend more space on the map than on the territory. It is not a defect. Metadata is what makes the data findable, comparable and recoverable. It is the reason I can ask a repository what changed last month and get an answer. But it is also the reason I check the size before I start a clone on a machine with a small disk. How I clone now A shallow clone takes the last version and leaves the history on the server. If I only want to read the lists, that is all I need, and the download becomes minutes instead of an afternoon. If I later want the history of one file, I can ask for exactly that file. I still keep the full clone of the repositories I care about, because reading old commits is the cheapest way to understand why a project is shaped the way it is. The trick is to decide before pressing enter, not after the disk is full.

blueteam_learning: Blue Team Learning The Sky is blue and in this site, is only me and you! Anyway, thank you for attacking my sites and teach me how to block your attacks. An honest thank you I mean it. Nobody teaches faster than someone who is trying to get inside without asking. In a few weeks I learned more about my own logs than in a year of reading about hardening, because the attacks told me which door of the house was visible from the street. The first lesson was that logs are not a record of what happened. They are a record of what somebody else was expecting to find. When the same path is requested a thousand times with three different user agents, that is not a visitor, that is a search. What this site gave them Nothing, and that is the point. There are no databases, no users, no sessions and no forms to fill. Everything here is static text, some images and a little music. An attacker who succeeds in reading a page has achieved what a browser achieves by existing. So the exercise was never about protecting data, it was about protecting attention: my attention, and the patience of a server that should answer readers instead of robots. What I learned to do Close what does not need to be open. Answer the scanners with the cheapest possible response. Read the difference between curiosity and automation. And accept that a public service is, by definition, visited by everything that is public, including the parts of the Internet that have no interest in the content at all. The Sky is blue, and in this site, is only me and you. Everybody else is just passing by with a script and a list.

bots: All Bots are welcome As you may see, this is a open source project and you can clone it and open a pull request. Sadly for your bots, I use Cloudflare, which is something that depend on them, not on me. ;) A bot is only a program with a schedule There is nothing evil in a bot. A crawler that reads this page to build an index, an archiver that keeps a copy for the future, a script that checks whether the site is still alive at three in the morning: all of those are polite, useful and welcome. They arrive once, they read, they leave, and they come back when it makes sense. The unfriendly part is never the automation, it is the control . When a thousand machines repeat the same request in the same second and none of them was invited, the site is not being read, it is being tested for weakness. The difference between a reader and an attack is not the tool, it is the intention behind the schedule. So nothing here is a secret The source of this blog is public. You can clone it, read it, fork it and open a pull request. If you find a spelling mistake, a broken link or a paragraph that makes no sense, tell me and I will be grateful. That is the whole point of working in the open: the correction is free and it arrives from someone who was paying attention. What is not public is the right to hammer the server. That decision is not mine anyway. Cloudflare decides which request is a browser and which request is a machine in a hurry, and I only see the result in the statistics. If your bot is challenged, it is not because I dislike bots, it is because the line between a crawler and a flood is thinner than it looks from the outside. What a bot can still do here Read the text. Follow the links. Take the RSS feed if you want the articles in your terminal. Keep a copy for an archive. Every one of those things is a compliment to a writer, and every one of those things costs almost nothing to serve. Just do not try to see how many requests per second the server can take. The answer is in the configuration, and the configuration is already boring. ;)

brutalBSD: Long Life OpenBSD \./ 2026-06-07 — — OpenBSD is the system I recommend when somebody asks me which one to read before which one to install. Not because it is easy, but because the documentation is honest. A manual that explains the whole system in the order in which the system boots is worth more than a thousand tutorials written by people who copied each other. This page is a tribute and a set of notes. It is not a guide, and it will not replace man afterboot . It exists because the first hour with a new system decides whether the person stays, and that hour is almost entirely made of reading. The Organic OpenBSD Library that I was trying to find in the web! Simplicity : "We gain Knowledge by reading small or big Books which sometimes make reference to other Books ." Being paranoid about security can be a little bit Evil , but if you find that others are trying to Break it, there is no Evil on it The question is: "If you wish to break some system, which best position you should be in? Inside or Outside?" OpenBSD ask some key tips for new users, like me or like you. Always use the more option and append the number of the email, to read the emails you will get on OpenBSD system by default. Is a Golden tip. Else you will only be able to read the last lines of your emails. For the first Welcome email, you lose all the necessary details to start, while you have access to all necessary details to participate, by sending your hw.sensors values. In case you use the correct option to read your emails, you figure out that OpenBSD creates a map of necessary steps and readings to start configuring the system, much better than any other BSD or Linux System. Their Welcome email, start to explain the very basics of using the man pages in the default Kshell and ask the user to type man afterboot , to start reading the first book, of many other books that are in the same Open Library , which is always Open , at any hour of any day and any night. Then it gives an example on how to install new packages using their Binary package manager, some extra notes and we start reading book after book. Sometimes in a exaustive experience, since they always link the necessary Books that are related to the one we are reading. All makes sense and there is no Hidden or secret knowledge, like what happen with FreeBSD man pages , when I was stucked on creating a disk file to use the VMs . In the other hand, OpenBSD vm manual pages, have the option to create those disk-files and all steps that are needed are explained the best they can, since we have access to the /etc/examples/* files that are not empty. By reading the afterboot book, you can know how everything is connected, how everything should work, what limitations exist, what security problems can happen, what can you do to prevent them, how to configure each service they have that are always Open , at any time of day or night. To me as a old Linux user, I always dream about this kind of approach, where there is a guide to start, which is available offline, in the shell, trying to prevent reading external resources, that can be old and useless, with options that don't exist in the -current version, creating misconfigurations and other possible problems to those who just follow along the steps that some articles describe, while I cannot deny, many awesome articles on the web about OpenBSD that are very useful, since they connect many services running at the same time, giving us a better understanding of how many services can run at the same time in peace. man security is just one of many books, that are refered in the afterboot Book. Not like any other BSD or Linux system, OpenBSD already try to secure your system, while you can hardener a bit more, even if you can update and patch your system when bugs or security issues are found and fixed with syspatch . If you think about Linux in general, You need to spend a lot of time to secure your system, while you need to understand how to configure a secure system without creating new problems on running some service, like what can happen with SELinux by being unable to login as root when testing and learning about that tecnology that looks simple but can be damn complex too. You are using a Firewall by default. You can create all kind of network.interfaces too. All tools that I knew from Linux, I can see a simple version on OpenBSD while being more rebust. Sadly, most of my computers have a NVIDIA GPU, and OpenBSD have no support, while I am not Linux gamer. My Windows machines are always secure because they are always and always were and always be, offline . No updates to break my Windows. They are perfect like that. Offline . Because my games run offline and if you physical access to them, you can only find games. I prefere papers for sensitive data. Libraries and Offices are always better when papers exist. Is just another "non-sense" evolution where companies and individuals Expose personal data on the web. The three commands that matter in the first hour Every new installation is a small panic. These three, in this order, replace the panic with a plan: man afterboot — the map. Read it once, slowly, with the machine beside you. man security — the list of what is already protected and what is still your responsibility. syspatch — the reminder that documentation does not patch a kernel. Run it, and run it again next week. What "brutal" actually means People call the OpenBSD documentation brutal because it does not try to be friendly. It does not congratulate you for opening a terminal. It does not produce a video. It gives you a sentence, precisely written, that stays true for the next ten years, and it assumes that you are capable of reading it. That is not brutality, that is respect. The brutal thing is the other model: a documentation that changes every six months, hides the important paragraph behind a newsletter form, and calls the reader a "user" while treating him like a lead. Where the philosophy touches the hardware The same idea appears in the code. A small base system, a firewall enabled by default, privilege separation everywhere, and a maintainer culture that prefers removing a feature to auditing it forever. You can disagree with the choices and still learn from the method: decide what the system must do, remove everything else, and write down the reason. My only real complaint is the one I have repeated many times in this blog: NVIDIA. Most of my machines carry one, and OpenBSD does not support the proprietary driver, so the tribute is written from a laptop that boots something else. A system can be excellent and still not be the system for your hardware. That is a fact about my desk, not about the project. Reading before installing If this page convinces you of one thing, let it be the order: read first, install second. The library is already on the machine, waiting behind a command, and it is the only library I know that opens at three in the morning, without a connection, and without asking who you are. ↑

bsdguide: Your FreeBSD Laptop — From Nothing to Locked-Down Desktop The total journey is ten steps plus appendices. You bring the laptop and one empty USB stick; this page brings everything else. Options you may skip are italic. Tips worth remembering appear underlined. FreeBSD features are bold. Step 0. what you will end up with At the end of this guide the laptop runs FreeBSD , a complete operating system assembled as one coherent base — kernel, drivers and tools versioned together — plus a desktop of your choosing, behind a pf firewall , on a ZFS disk with TRIM, using doas for admin powers instead of ever logging in as root, and finally locked so nobody can change it without the admin password — not even by booting another kernel. This machine's parts are FreeBSD-friendly: the Iris Xe works through i915kms , the AX201 Wi-Fi through iwlwifi , the I219-V network chip through em — all native or one package away. Hardware What FreeBSD does with it i7-11390H, 8 threads native support ; powerd governs clocks Iris Xe graphics drm-kmod package → i915kms AX201 Wi-Fi 6 iwlwifi(4) driver + firmware pkg I219-V ethernet em(4) , fully native NVMe SSD ZFS with native TRIM + compression The only unrecoverable step is Step 1: everything currently on the laptop's disk will be erased. Move what matters to another machine or account before continuing. Step 1. make the install stick Download the current RELEASE memstick image — pick amd64-memstick.img.xz . A RELEASE build is the stable-and-patched choice; newer branches exist and are covered in Appendix D. Write the image to a USB stick of 4 GB or more (everything on it is lost). From Windows use balenaEtcher ; from Linux: unxz FreeBSD-14.3-RELEASE-amd64-memstick.img.xz dd if=FreeBSD-14.3-RELEASE-amd64-memstick.img of=/dev/sdX bs=1M conv=sync status=progress Always point dd at the whole stick ( /dev/sdX ), never at a partition like /dev/sdX1 . Verify the copy: cmp /dev/sdX image.img — a silent cmp is the difference between a working installer and a random hang halfway through. Boot it: tap the boot-menu key ( F12 / F2 / ESC ), choose the UEFI: USB entry. The official Handbook installation chapter has imagery for every screen. Step 2. install: root filesystem on ZFS, encrypted Installer menu: Install . Keyboard: your layout — pt was pre-set to match. Hostname: freebsd-desktop — a neutral hostname keeps every network log from carrying your real name. Partitioning: ZFS , Stripe (single SSD; a mirror needs two drives), enable encryption with a passphrase — foundation of Appendix F. Target disk: the internal NVMe only . The USB stick itself appears as da0 — selecting it destroys the installer. Root password; then add your user to the wheel group — wheel is what doas.conf will authorize (Step 6). Networking: enter Wi-Fi name/password; the installer writes wpa_supplicant.conf for you. Cable users pick em0; both are configured in Step 3. Reboot and remove the stick. Step 3. root system settings — rc.conf The rc.conf file is the switchboard : one line per service, interface, behavior. Merge the lines below or paste into /etc/rc.conf learning each as you go: # /etc/rc.conf — desktop laptop: i7-11390H (Tiger Lake, Iris Xe), AX201 Wi-Fi, I219 Ethernet, HDA audio # Merge into the installed system's /etc/rc.conf with post-install.sh (does NOT overwrite). # ----- General ----- hostname="freebsd-desktop" # change to taste keymap="pt" # Portuguese console keymap; adjust if different clear_tmp_enable="YES" syslogd_flags="-ss" # do not open a remote syslog socket sendmail_enable="NONE" update_motd="NO" # less boot noise; set YES if you want MOTD # ----- Graphics: Intel Tiger Lake (UHD/Iris Xe Gen12) through drm-kmod ----- kld_list="i915kms" # ----- Networking: onboard Intel Ethernet (I219-V) ----- defaultroute_delay="0" # don't stall boot waiting for DHCP ifconfig_em0="DHCP" # rename with: ifconfig -l # ----- Wi-Fi: Intel AX201 (iwlwifi, 802.11ax) ----- wlans_iwlwifi0="wlan0" create_args_wlan0="wlandev iwlwifi0" # Prefer Wi-Fi as default route; remove em0 line above if fully wireless: # ifconfig_wlan0="WPA SYNCDHCP" ifconfig_wlan0="WPA SYNCDHCP country PT" # regdomain helps 5GHz channel power/X # ----- Firewall: pf (enabled; ruleset ships as pf.conf) ----- pf_enable="YES" pf_rules="/etc/pf.conf" pflog_enable="YES" pflog_logfile="/var/log/pflog" # Uncomment if you later run jails behind NAT: # pf_flags="" # (empty — ruleset handles everything) # ----- Jails (optional — uncomment the block to use the bridge below) ----- # Jail bridge: keeps internal jail traffic off your LAN segment. # Create it once: # ifconfig bridge0 create cloned_interfaces="bridge0" # bridge for jail networking (uncomment-free option, see pf.conf) ifconfig_bridge0="inet 10.0.100.1/24 descr 'jail bridge'" # host side ifconfig_bridge0_member="em0" # comment out if you want a NAT-only bridge (see pf.conf) # Explanation: # * With bridge0_member=em0 the jail VMs appear on the LAN (bridged mode). # * Without it you must NAT via pf (see "NAT for jails" inside pf.conf). autobridge_enable="YES" # auto-populate bridge0 members on boot autobridge_interfaces="bridge0" # ----- Services ----- dbus_enable="YES" moused_enable="YES" powerd_enable="YES" powerd_flags="-a hiadaptive -b adaptive -n adaptive" # CPU freq scaling on AC/battery # ----- Display manager + misc hardware ----- sddm_enable="YES" # graphical login manager (SDDM) cups_enable="NO" # set YES if you need printing avahi_daemon_enable="NO" avahi_dnsconfd_enable="NO" # ----- Optional: sshd for remote management of the laptop and jails ----- # sshd_enable="YES" # uncomment only if you actually need SSH # ----- Local scripts ----- # Nothing custom needed for this hardware. Step 4. boot-time settings — loader.conf loader.conf runs before the kernel : it loads modules too early for later, sets console resolution. Two values matter most — zfs_load (root filesystem) and the framebuffer. ARC cap (Appendix B) and the loader password (Appendix F) also live here. # /boot/loader.conf — i7-11390H (Tiger Lake) laptop, desktop use # Merge into /boot/loader.conf on the installed system (post-install.sh handles it). # ----- Kernel modules (GPU firmware must be installed via pkg first: drm-kmod) ----- # i915kms is loaded from rc.conf kld_list instead; keep that as the single source. # ----- Filesystem ----- zfs_load="YES" # if you installed on ZFS; harmless otherwise # tmpfs_load="YES" # default in GENERIC already # ----- Console / framebuffer ----- kern.vt.fb.default_width="1920" kern.vt.fb.default_height="1080" kern.vt.fb.default_depth="32" # ----- Power management (Tiger Lake laptop) ----- hint.p4tcc.0.disabled="0" hint.acpi_throttle.0.disabled="0" hint.apm.0.disabled="1" performance_cx_lowest="Cmax" economy_cx_lowest="Cmax" kern.sched.idle_cnt=1 # ----- Misc ----- kern.geom.label.gptid.enable="0" # shorter device names in glabel; cosmetic autoboot_delay="3" Step 5. kernel behavior — sysctl.conf Sysctls are kernel knobs , most adjustable without reboot ( sysctl -n key prints current value). This set sizes network buffers for the AX201's Wi-Fi 6, loosens shared-memory limits for browsers and GIMP, keeps interaction snappy. Jail forwarding/bridge knobs wait commented at the bottom. # /etc/sysctl.conf — desktop laptop tuning (safe, generic) # Merge into /etc/sysctl.conf on the installed system (post-install.sh handles it). # ----- Desktop responsiveness (interactive scheduling) ----- kern.sched.preempt_thresh=224 # wake CPU-bound tasks earlier for interactive apps # ----- Multimedia: raise shared memory limits for browsers/desktops ----- kern.ipc.shmmax=134217728 # 128 MB shared memory segment (browsers, GIMP) kern.ipc.shmall=32768 # pages for shared memory # ----- Local IPC (X11/wayland sockets, pipe-heavy tiling setups) ----- net.local.stream.sendspace=65536 net.local.stream.recvspace=65536 net.local.dgram.maxdgram=16384 net.local.dgram.recvspace=65536 # ----- VM / cache behavior: favor desktop interactivity over huge caches ----- vm.swappiness=10 # prefer RAM over swap (laptop with 16-32GB) # NOTE: no vm dirty-page tuning here — defaults are well balanced on 14.x # ----- Network stack (client desktop, not server) ----- kern.ipc.maxsockbuf=4194304 # larger TCP buffers for fast Wi-Fi 6 (AX201) net.inet.tcp.recvbuf_max=2097152 net.inet.tcp.sendbuf_max=2097152 net.inet.tcp.recvspace=131072 net.inet.tcp.sendspace=131072 net.inet.tcp.rfc1323=1 # window scaling — required for Wi-Fi 6 throughput net.inet.tcp.delayed_ack=0 # lower latency for interactive traffic net.inet.tcp.syncookies=1 # SYN protection in combination with pf net.inet.udp.recvspace=65536 net.inet.udp.max_dgram=57344 # ----- ICMP: respond (useful on LAN) but rate-limit ----- net.inet.icmp.icmplim=200 # ----- Sysctl for pf with jails (uncomment when jail block is used) ----- # net.inet.ip.forwarding=1 # REQUIRED if host NATs for jails (pf nat) # net.link.bridge.pfil_member=0 # filter on bridge, not member interfaces # net.link.bridge.pfil_bridge=1 # pf applies to bridge0 traffic # net.inet6.ip6.forwarding=1 # only if you give jails IPv6 # ----- Sound (HDA): use the right default unit if needed ----- # hw.snd.default_unit=0 # hw.snd.default_driver=dsp Step 6. admin rights without root logins — doas.conf doas is how you exercise admin power — doas prefix, your password once per session, root powers for one command. This file authorizes the wheel group. Every use lands in auth.log — no habit of staying root. # /usr/local/etc/doas.conf — replace `youruser` with your actual login name # permit :wheel permit nopass :wheel permit keepenv :wheel Step 7. the firewall — pf.conf pf is a stateful kernel firewall : every outbound allowed quietly, inbound refused and logged , plus — as comments, ready to uncomment — complete jail networking scenarios : bridged onto LAN, hidden behind NAT, jail-to-jail DMZ, VNET. The numbered comments in its §10 are the debugging commands that save you when a rule misfires. Default state is already correct for a laptop: nothing to uncomment on day one. # ========================================================================== # pf.conf — FreeBSD desktop laptop: i7-11390H (Tiger Lake) # ========================================================================== # Install to: /etc/pf.conf # Enable: service pf start (enabled via rc.conf pf_enable="YES") # Test ruleset: doas pfctl -nf /etc/pf.conf (syntax check, do NOT load) # Load ruleset: doas pfctl -f /etc/pf.conf # View rules: doas pfctl -sr # Live log: doas tcpdump -n -e -ttt -i pflog0 # # DESIGN GOAL # * Laptop used as a normal desktop => default deny inbound, allow outbound # on everything. This alone gives you a solid, quiet firewall. # * Big commented blocks below show step-by-step how to extend it for JAILS # (bridge mode, NAT mode, per-jail rules, jail-to-jail traffic). Each # option is a comment: uncomment only the lines you need. # # NOTE ON SYNTAX: this uses $uplink (an interface-list macro) instead of the # OpenBSD-only "egress" group keyword, so it works on FreeBSD pf as shipped. # ========================================================================== # -------------------------------------------------------------------------- # 0. MACROS — edit these to match your setup (run `ifconfig` to check names) # -------------------------------------------------------------------------- # em0 = Intel I219-V Ethernet (built in) # wlan0 = Intel AX201 Wi-Fi # bridge0 = jail bridge (see rc.conf cloned_interfaces) ext_if = "em0" # wired uplink (comment out if wifi-only) wifi_if = "wlan0" # wireless uplink jb_if = "bridge0" # jail bridge # Uplink group: rules match whichever interface exists/is active. # (pf accepts an inactive interface in a macro without complaining.) uplink = "{" $ext_if $wifi_if "}" # -------------------------------------------------------------------------- # 1. GLOBAL OPTIONS # -------------------------------------------------------------------------- set skip on lo0 # If you later trust ALL jails on this host, stop filtering their bridge: # set skip on $jb_if set limit { states 200000, frags 50000, src-nodes 50000 } set loginterface $ext_if # "normal" is right for a desktop. "aggressive" drops idle states sooner — # sensible on battery with a 4G/phone hotspot, not needed at home. set optimization normal set block-policy return # send TCP RST instead of silent drop set state-policy if-bound # states bound to the interface that made them # -------------------------------------------------------------------------- # 2. NORMALIZATION # -------------------------------------------------------------------------- # Reassemble fragments; clamp MSS so tunnels/PPPoE can't blackhole traffic. scrub in all max-mss 1440 fragment reassemble # On a plain home LAN you can reduce it to just: # scrub in all # -------------------------------------------------------------------------- # 3. DEFAULT POLICY + LOGGING # -------------------------------------------------------------------------- # Default deny, logged to pflog0 (see tcpdump command in the header). block log all # -------------------------------------------------------------------------- # 4. LOOPBACK & BASIC PROTOCOLS # -------------------------------------------------------------------------- pass quick on lo0 all # ICMP: keep ping working but rate-limited, out unrestricted. pass in on $uplink inet proto icmp icmp-type 8 keep state (max 100, source-track rule) pass out inet proto icmp keep state # ICMP6 is REQUIRED for IPv6 to work at all (ND/RA are carried in ICMP6). pass in on $uplink inet6 proto icmp6 icmp6-type { echoreq unreach timex } pass out inet6 proto icmp6 keep state # Option: total IPv6-off switch (uncomment BOTH lines, comment the two # icmp6 "pass in/out" lines above): # block drop in on $uplink inet6 all # block drop out on $uplink inet6 all # -------------------------------------------------------------------------- # 5. OUTBOUND: allow the desktop to reach anywhere # -------------------------------------------------------------------------- # The one rule that gives a desktop its freedom: pass out on $uplink inet all keep state # If you prefer a TIGHT whitelist instead, comment out the rule above and # uncomment these (leave NTP/DHCP lines below alone): #pass out on $uplink inet proto tcp to port { 80 443 853 } keep state #pass out on $uplink inet proto udp to port { 53 443 } keep state # DoH/QUIC # Keep these two regardless of policy — time + DHCP are infrastructure: pass out on $uplink inet proto udp to port 123 keep state # NTP pass out on $uplink inet proto udp from any port 68 to any port 67 keep state # DHCP # -------------------------------------------------------------------------- # 6. buddhismManual: Skip to the manual Monkey Blog · Research Manual · 佛法 The Sound of Emptiness 空 之 聲 A working manual of Buddhism: the Buddha and the four truths, dependent origination, the canons and the schools, emptiness and mind, meditation, the great mantras syllable by syllable, the sutras and their key passages, chant, symbols, ethics, death, and the long argument about what any of it means. OdicforceSounds In English Twenty chapters Pali · Sanskrit · Chinese 學 學 How to read this manual Buddhism is not one thing. It is a family of traditions two and a half millennia old, spread from Afghanistan to Japan, written in at least six languages, and split by arguments that are still live. This manual keeps the layers apart so that the whole can be seen. The first layer is the early teaching preserved in Pali and in Chinese and Tibetan parallels: the four truths, dependent origination, the eightfold path, the discipline of the monks. The second is the Mahayana expansion, from roughly the first century BCE: the bodhisattva ideal, emptiness, buddha-nature, vast sutras and a cosmos full of Buddhas. The third is the tantric or Vajrayana layer from the sixth century CE onward: initiation, deity yoga, mandala and mantra, in Tibet, Japan and parts of China. The fourth is the modern layer: colonial scholarship, Theosophy, the mindfulness industry, secular Buddhism. Two rules First: a text's age is not its authority. The Pali canon is older than the Lotus Sutra; that makes it earlier, not truer. Second: the tradition itself knows its texts were composed over centuries, and has its own explanation — upāya , skilful means, and the idea that a Buddha teaches what a given audience can hear. Languages matter. Pali is the Middle Indo-Aryan language of the Theravada canon; Sanskrit is the cosmopolitan language of the Mahayana and the tantras; Chinese and Tibetan are the two great translation canons; Japanese and Korean carry their own transmissions. A term like dukkha appears in this manual with its Pali form, and Sanskrit equivalents where they differ ( duḥkha in Sanskrit, 苦 in Chinese). This is a descriptive manual. It is not a creed, not an initiation, and not medical or psychological advice. Where the tradition makes empirical claims — about rebirth, about the effects of meditation, about the cosmos — the text says what is claimed and what can be checked. The reader is trusted with the difference. One thread connects this manual to the rest of the site: the Buddhist Monkey . The Monkey King Sun Wukong is a Buddhist literary figure — the pilgrim who escorts Xuanzang west to fetch sutras in Journey to the West — and OdicforceSounds has long used the Monkey as the figure of a mind that cannot sit still. That monkey is the reader of this manual: curious, impatient, and occasionally enlightened by accident. 佛 佛 The Buddha and the story 佛陀 fótuó is not a name but a title: buddha , "one who has awakened". The historical teacher was Siddhattha Gotama in Pali, Siddhārtha Gautama in Sanskrit, of the Sakya clan — which is why he is called Sakyamuni , the sage of the Sakyas. The dates are disputed. The tradition's long chronology puts him at 563–483 BCE; most modern scholars prefer something like 480–400 BCE, with the death somewhere near 400. He was born at Lumbini, in what is now Nepal, raised at Kapilavatthu, and, according to the story, kept inside a palace by a father who wanted him to be a king rather than a renunciant. The four sights The story turns on a chariot ride. Sheltered prince meets, in succession, an old man, a sick man, a corpse, and a wandering ascetic who looks at ease. The first three teach him that the body is a loan; the fourth shows a way of living with that knowledge. He leaves the palace, studies with two teachers of absorption, masters their attainments, finds them insufficient, and spends years in extreme austerity until he is nearly dead. Then a memory — as a boy, under a rose-apple tree, he had entered a natural state of calm — suggests that the body is not the enemy. He takes food, sits under a pipal tree at Bodh Gaya, and resolves not to rise until he understands. The night is described as a battle with Māra, the tempter and lord of the sense-realm: armies, daughters, the offer of a kingdom. He touches the earth as witness, and by dawn he is awake. What "awake" means here Not omniscience about everything, but the end of the three fermentations: sensual desire, becoming, and ignorance. The traditional formula is that he knew suffering, its arising, its cessation, and the path — which is to say, the four truths, seen not as propositions but as tasks completed. He teaches for about forty-five years. The first sermon, at the deer park at Sarnath, is the Dhammacakkappavattana Sutta , "the turning of the wheel of dharma": the middle way, the four truths, the eightfold path. His last words, in the Mahāparinibbāna Sutta , are a warning against relying on a person: Mahāparinibbāna Sutta · Pali “Handa dāni, bhikkhave, āmantayāmi vo: vayadhammā saṅkhārā, appamādena sampādetha.” “Come now, monks, I address you: all conditioned things decay. Strive on with diligence.” Dīgha Nikāya 16 He is not a god in the early texts, and he discourages a cult of his person. Asked what should happen after his death, he says: do not worry about the funeral, practise. The relics and the stupa come later, and become one of the great engines of the tradition. Buddhas before and after The early texts already have previous Buddhas — Vipassī, Sikhī, Vessabhū, Kakusandha, Koṇāgamana, Kassapa — and a future one, Metteyya (Maitreya), who waits in the Tuṣita heaven. The pattern matters more than the names: awakening is not a one-off event in history but a recurring possibility, and the dharma is rediscovered each time it is lost. The biographical genre grows enormously. The Buddhacarita of Aśvaghoṣa (2nd century CE) is a Sanskrit epic; the Pali Jātaka tales give hundreds of previous lives; the Lalitavistara adds the miracles. The story as most of Asia knows it is a composite, and it is meant to be contemplated, not fact-checked like a newspaper. 若見諸相非相，即見如來 If you see all appearances as no-appearance, you see the Tathāgata. The image is a wheel whose axle does not fit — duḥ , bad, plus kha , the hole. Even pleasure is dukkha in the sense that it cannot last and leaves a hunger behind it. The eightfold path The path is usually grouped into three trainings — ethics ( sīla ), concentration ( samādhi ) and wisdom ( paññā ) — and the order is a spiral rather than a ladder: right view guides the rest, and the rest clarifies right view. 八正道 — the noble eightfold path Factor Pali What it means in practice 正見 sammā-diṭṭhi seeing the four truths, karma and impermanence as they apply to this life 正思惟 sammā-saṅkappa intention free of sensuality, ill will and cruelty 正語 sammā-vācā no lying, divisive speech, harsh speech or idle chatter 正業 sammā-kammanta no killing, stealing or sexual misconduct 正命 sammā-ājīva a livelihood that does not require harming others 正精進 sammā-vāyāma cultivating good states and abandoning unwholesome ones 正念 sammā-sati mindfulness of body, feeling, mind and phenomena 正定 sammā-samādhi the four absorptions ( jhāna ), unified and translucent Two parables keep the path from becoming an ideology. The raft : the dharma is a raft for crossing, not a possession to carry on your head — even the teaching is to be let go when it has done its work. The arrow : a man shot by an arrow refuses treatment until he knows the archer's name, clan, height and the kind of bow; he dies before the answers arrive. The unanswered metaphysical questions ( avyākata ) — is the world eternal? is it finite? is the self the body? — are set aside not because they are forbidden but because they do not help with the arrow. 諸惡莫作，眾善奉行，自淨其意，是諸佛教 Not doing any evil, undertaking the good, purifying one's mind — this is the teaching of the Buddhas. Dhammapada 183 緣 緣起 Impermanence, no-self, karma Three observations are said to cover all conditioned things: anicca , they change; dukkha , they cannot satisfy; anattā , they are not a self. The third is the one Western readers find hardest, and the one the tradition insists on. The five aggregates What we call "I" is analysed into five heaps — not parts of a self, but processes that a self is imputed to: rūpa — form, the body and the material world. vedanā — feeling-tone: pleasant, unpleasant, neutral. saññā — perception, the labelling that recognises. saṅkhārā — formations: volition, habit, the constructing mind. viññāṇa — consciousness, the knowing of each sense door. The argument is not "there is no person". It is that nothing in the heap is permanent, and nothing in it is ownerless of change, so nothing in it deserves the name "self" in the sense of an unchanging essence. The person remains — as a process, a stream, a convention. Dependent origination 緣起 paṭicca-samuppāda is the central doctrine, older in feel than the four truths and arguably deeper: when this is, that is; with the arising of this, that arises. Este documento compara as regras e não os feriados: os quatro tipos de calendário, as festas que deles dependem, as janelas em que caem e os cinco erros que se cometem ao traduzir uma data. OdicforceSounds Em Português Treze capítulos Regras, não datas ☾ Como ler este calendário Este documento não é uma lista de feriados. É um mapa de regras : cada tradição conta o tempo com um relógio diferente, e a maior parte das confusões sobre datas sagradas vem de converter um relógio no outro sem dizer qual está a ser usado. A regra de leitura é esta: procura primeiro a linha do calendário (solar, lunar, lunissolar ou litúrgico), depois a janela em que a festa cai, e só no fim a data concreta — que muda todos os anos e que nunca deve ser copiada de um sítio sem verificação. Onde a página diz «aproximado», é aproximado de propósito. Aviso de precisão Nenhuma data deste documento está calculada para um ano específico. As janelas são estáveis; as datas não. Para publicar uma data, calcula-a a partir da regra e cita a autoridade que a fixou — nunca de uma lista de «feriados 2026» encontrada por acaso. ☉ Quatro relógios Uma tradição não «segue o calendário»: escolhe o que observar no céu. Há quatro respostas possíveis, e cada uma produz um tipo diferente de ano. Os quatro tipos de calendário Tipo Observa Ano Consequência Tradições Solar Sol — solstícios e equinócios 365 dias, com correcção bissexta As festas caem sempre na mesma estação Gregoriano, persa (Nowruz), calendários litúrgicos ocidentais Lunar Lua — meses de 29 ou 30 dias ~354 dias As festas deslizam ~11 dias por ano solar Islâmico (Hijri) Lunissolar Lua, com meses intercalares para acertar o Sol 354 dias + mês extra em 7 de cada 19 anos As festas ficam na mesma estação e mudam de dia Chinês, hebraico, hindu, budista do sul e do leste Litúrgico Uma âncora móvel e uma contagem de semanas Variável Toda a liturgia se reorganiza em torno da Páscoa Cristianismo ocidental e oriental O calendário lunissolar é o mais engenhoso e o mais mal compreendido: para que o Ano Novo chinês não ande pelo ano, acrescenta-se um décimo terceiro mês em sete anos de cada dezanove. Não é um erro de contagem — é uma correcção embutida. ✝ O ano cristão: a Páscoa manda O calendário cristão ocidental é solar, mas tem uma âncora móvel. A Páscoa é o primeiro domingo depois da primeira lua cheia eclesiástica a partir do equinócio de 21 de março — e tudo o que é móvel depende dela. É o exemplo mais claro de que «a mesma religião» não implica «o mesmo calendário». ☪ O ano islâmico: o deslizar O calendário Hijri é estritamente lunar: doze meses de 29 ou 30 dias, ~354 dias por ano. O resultado é que cada festa percorre o ano solar em cerca de trinta e três anos. Ramadão — o nono mês, jejum do nascer ao pôr do sol. Chega ~11 dias mais cedo a cada ano. Eid al-Fitr — o fim do jejum, no primeiro dia de Shawwal. Eid al-Adha — a festa do sacrifício, no décimo dia de Dhu al-Hijja, ligada à peregrinação. Ashura — o décimo dia de Muharram, com significados distintos para sunitas e xiitas. Mawlid — o nascimento do Profeta, no terceiro mês; não é universalmente celebrado. O início de cada mês depende tradicionalmente da observação da lua nova, o que significa que a data pode variar um dia entre países e entre comunidades dentro do mesmo país. Qualquer calendário que apresente o Ramadão como uma data única está a esconder essa variação — não a simplificá-la. Escreve a regra, indica a janela, e diz quem a fixou naquele ano. 春 O ano chinês: dois relógios num só O calendário tradicional chinês é lunissolar, com vinte e quatro termos solares por cima dos meses lunares. As festas vivem nos dois níveis — e é isso que as torna difíceis de traduzir. Written from the classical texts, the commentaries and the later systems — and kept honest about which is which. OdicforceSounds In English Twenty chapters No doctrine 學 學 How to read this manual Three thousand years of Chinese reflection on the sacred produced several overlapping systems, not one. This manual keeps them apart so that you can see how they fit: classical philosophy, calendrical cosmology, divination, medicine, alchemy, and the later syntheses that turn all of it into a single correspondential machine. The classical layer is the oldest and the least systematic: the Daodejing (c. 4th–3rd century BCE), the Zhuangzi , the Yijing and its early commentaries. The Han layer (2nd century BCE – 2nd century CE) is where the five phases, yin-yang and the calendar are welded into a state cosmology. The religious layer is the organised Daoism of the 2nd century CE onward, with its liturgies, gods, body-gods and alchemy. The Song–Ming layer is the neo-Confucian synthesis of Zhou Dunyi and Zhu Xi, which still shapes how most people — Chinese and Western — read the material today. And the modern layer is the twentieth-century export: Jung, Wilhelm, "Tao of Physics", wellness branding. A working rule When a claim appears in this manual, ask which layer it comes from. "The five phases explain the seasons" is Han cosmology. "Qi flows in meridians" is the medical tradition. "Qi is a measurable biofield" is a modern claim that the classical texts do not make and that physics has not found. What follows is descriptive and comparative. The systems are coherent on their own terms and have real explanatory power inside a symbolic register — which is not the same as being empirically true. Nothing here is medical, psychological or financial advice, and no ritual instruction requires you to fast, ingest anything, or pay anyone. Characters are given in traditional forms, with pinyin. Dates are approximate; the Chinese material is layered and often pseudepigraphic. Tables are the skeleton of every system — read them before the prose. Repetition is deliberate: each system re-reads the last one. 道 道 The way and its power 道 dào is a road, a method, a way of speaking and a way of being. In the classical texts it is less a god than the grain of things: what makes a path walkable and a life coherent. The character is written 辶 (walk) plus 首 (head): the traditional analysis treats the first as semantic and the second as phonetic. The oldest senses are concrete — a road, a direction, a technique — and the philosophical sense grows out of them rather than replacing them. This matters: in the Daodejing the way is still spoken of as something you walk, not something you believe. The opening lines set the problem: 道可道，非常道 — "the way that can be spoken is not the constant way." Not a prohibition on speech (the book then speaks for five thousand characters) but a warning that any formulation is a fence. Chapter 25 gives the famous ladder: 人法地，地法天，天法道，道法自然 — humans follow earth, earth follows heaven, heaven follows the way, the way follows ziran , "its own so-ness." 德 dé Power, virtue, the gift that a thing receives from the way and can therefore do. Often rendered "virtue", but it is closer to efficacy: what a thing is able to be. 自然 zìrán Self-so, spontaneity, "of itself". Not "nature" as scenery; the way things are when nothing is forced. 無為 wúwéi Non-coercive action: acting without meddling, in season, so that the action does not leave a bruise. Not doing nothing. 樸 pǔ The uncarved block: the state before naming and carving. A political ideal as much as a personal one. 反 fǎn Return, and also "contrary". The way moves by reversal: what goes out returns, extremes turn. 玄 xuán Dark, deep, mysterious — the colour of what has not yet been distinguished. The manual's second title-word. Wuwei is not passivity The Zhuangzi gives the image that makes the idea concrete: Cook Ding butchers an ox for Lord Wenhui. His blade has no edge left, because he does not hack through joints — he finds the gaps. 依乎天理 , "following the grain of heaven." The skill is total, the effort is not. That is wuwei: competence so complete that it stops looking like effort, applied where the situation is already opening. The political reading is blunter. The ruler who legislates every detail creates the disorder he fears; the ruler who sets the season and steps back lets the village work. Chapter 57 puts it as a paradox — the more prohibitions, the more thieves — and Chapter 60 as a kitchen rule: govern a great state as you would fry a small fish, which is to say, do not keep turning it. 為學日益，為道日損 In learning, every day add. In the way, every day subtract. wéi xué rì yì, wéi dào rì sǔn — Daodejing 48 The way is in the low places Asked where the way is, Zhuangzi answers: in the ant. Lower: in the weed. Lower still: in the broken tile. And then, in a line that has kept its shock for two thousand years, in shit. The point is not provocation but consistency: if the way is everywhere, it cannot prefer the palace. The Daodejing makes the same move with water, the valley, and the uncarved block — the low, the soft, the unnamed. Two readings of the way have coexisted since the beginning. One is mystical: the way is ineffable, and the texts circle it with negations. The other is naturalistic: the way is the regular order of the world, discoverable in seasons, rivers and bodies. Most classical passages can be read either way; the later traditions chose sides, and so do modern readers. 極 極 From no-pole to ten thousand things Chinese cosmology is generative arithmetic: nothing, one, two, three, the four images, the eight trigrams, the ten thousand things. Each step is a differentiation, not a creation ex nihilo. The Daodejing , chapter 42, gives the compact formula: 道生一，一生二，二生三，三生萬物 — the way produces one, one produces two, two produces three, three produces the ten thousand things. The next line explains the physics of it: 萬物負陰而抱陽，沖氣以為和 — the ten thousand things carry yin on their backs and embrace yang, and the blending of qi makes harmony. The "three" is usually read as yin, yang and the harmony between them; or heaven, earth and humanity; or the two plus the breath that moves between. The later diagram tradition, systematised by Zhou Dunyi in the eleventh century, gives the sequence in diagram form: 無極 wújí — no pole: the limitless, before any axis. 太極 tàijí — the great pole: the single point in which movement and stillness are still one. 兩儀 liǎngyí — the two modes: yin and yang. 四象 sìxiàng — the four images: old yang, young yang, young yin, old yin (the four possible pairs of lines). 八卦 bāguà — the eight trigrams: three-line figures, each a situation. 萬物 wànwù — the ten thousand things: the world as it can be named. The older mythic register gives the same structure a body. In the Pangu 盤古 story, first attested around the third century CE, the primordial giant dies and his body becomes the world: breath becomes wind and clouds, voice becomes thunder, eyes become sun and moon, blood the rivers, hair the trees, and the parasites of his body become people. It is a late myth, not a classical one, but it expresses something the manuals keep repeating: the world is a body, and a body is a landscape . Why the numbers matter The sequence 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 8, 64 is not decoration. It is a compression scheme: each number marks a class of distinctions that later systems can reuse. One is unity, two is polarity, three is relation, four is orientation, five is process, eight is situation, sixty-four is the full set of situations. A manual that knows the numbers can navigate the tables without memorising them. Hundun 混沌 , the unformed, is the other name for the beginning: a lump, a broth, a darkness without holes. In one famous Zhuangzi story the emperor of the centre, Hundun, is kind to the emperors of the north and south; to repay him they bore him seven holes — eyes, ears, nostrils, mouth — one a day, and on the seventh day he dies. The story is about the cost of making a thing legible. It is also, quietly, a creation myth in reverse. 陰 陰陽 Yin and yang The words are geographical before they are metaphysical: 陰 is the shaded side of a hill, 陽 the sunny side. Everything else — dark and light, cold and hot, receptive and active, earth and heaven — is an extension of that first observation. Both characters share the mound radical 阜 (written 阝 on the left): the image is a slope. The oldest forms add a phonetic element, and the meaning is relational — a side, not a substance. This is why yin-yang is not a list of two things but a way of describing any pair as aspects of one situation. The four relations Opposition — they are distinct and pull apart. Interdependence — neither exists alone; no shadow without a light. Consumption — as one waxes the other wanes; the seasons are the model. Conversion — at the extreme each becomes the other; noon becomes afternoon, summer turns to autumn. The classic diagram (the "taiji tu", drawn above) is often read as a static balance. It is not. The S-curve is a rotation, and each fish carries a dot of its opposite: the seed of the other at the heart of each phase. A static equilibrium would not need the dots. The diagram's modern form is relatively late — the familiar paired-fish version spreads in the Ming — but the logic is classical. 一陰一陽之謂道 One yin, one yang — that is what is called the way. yī yīn yī yáng zhī wèi dào — Yizhuan, Xici What yin-yang is not It is not a moral hierarchy, though it has been used as one. In Han political cosmology yang is the ruler, yin the minister; yang the husband, yin the wife; and the pairing was used to naturalise subordination. That usage is historical, not inherent: the same pair is used in medicine to describe two patterns that both need treating, and in the Yijing the yin line is not inferior but receptive — the condition of anything being received. Nor is it a scientific dualism. In Chinese medicine, yin and yang are diagnostic shorthand for clusters of signs (cold, slow, pale versus hot, restless, red) and treatment aims at relation, not at "increasing the yin" in any measurable quantity. The pattern is the point. 五 五行 The five phases 五行 wǔxíng is usually translated "five elements". A better rendering is five goings or five stages — 行 means to move, to go, a course. They are processes in a cycle, not substances in a jar. The comparison with the Greek four elements misleads. Earth, air, fire and water are building materials; wood, fire, earth, metal and water are phases of a transformation, each defined by what it does to the others. Fire is not a stuff but an upward, heating movement; water is a downward, cooling one; metal is contraction; wood is expansion; earth is the turning point where one phase hands over to the next. The two cycles Generating 生 shēng — each phase produces the next: wood → fire → earth → metal → water → wood. It is the cycle of nourishment and growth, used for families, seasons and support. Controlling 克 kè — each phase restrains another: wood → earth, earth → water, water → fire, fire → metal, metal → wood. It is the cycle of regulation, used for discipline and for explaining disease when the restraint goes too far: 乘 chéng , over-acting, and 侮 wǔ , insulting — when the controlled phase turns on its controller. The table is the single most reused object in Chinese symbolic thought: medicine, music, feng shui, calendar, cuisine, politics and poetry all draw from it. Where the system strains A correspondential system works by analogy, and analogy is cheap: anything can be mapped onto anything with enough ingenuity. Its strength is integration — one table explains the seasons, the organs and the notes together. Its weakness is unfalsifiability: a mismatch is explained by an extra rule (over-acting, insulting, a hidden phase) rather than by dropping the model. Treat the table as a grammar, not as a lab result. 卦 八卦 The eight trigrams A trigram is three lines, each either solid (yang) or broken (yin). Eight are possible, and together they are the alphabet of Chinese cosmology: heaven and earth, thunder and wind, water and fire, mountain and lake. 卦 guà , the word for a hexagram or trigram, is written with the doubled earth radical — a picture of something hung up, displayed, a sign. The tradition attributes the trigrams to Fuxi 伏羲 , a culture hero who is said to have seen them on the back of a turtle emerging from the river, or in the patterns of the sky. Historically they are Bronze Age divination marks; the attribution is legend, and useful as legend. The eight trigrams: image, attribute, family, direction, phase Name Image Attribute Family Later Heaven Phase ☰ 乾 qián heaven strength, creativity father north-west metal ☱ 兌 duì lake, marsh joy, pleasure youngest daughter west metal ☲ 離 lí fire clinging, brightness middle daughter south fire ☳ 震 zhèn thunder arousing, movement eldest son east wood ☴ 巽 xùn wind, wood penetrating eldest daughter south-east wood ☵ 坎 kǎn water, pit abysmal, danger middle son north water ☶ 艮 gèn mountain stillness, stopping youngest son north-east earth ☷ 坤 kūn earth devotion, yielding mother south-west earth Read the lines from the bottom up. ☰ is three solid lines; ☷ is three broken. The middle line is the trigram's centre of gravity: a single solid line between two broken ones ( ☵ ) is water, the light trapped in the dark; a single broken line between two solid ones ( ☲ ) is fire, the dark held inside brightness. That symmetry is the whole system in miniature. Two arrangements The Earlier Heaven sequence, attributed to Fuxi, places heaven in the south and earth in the north, fire in the east and water in the west — a map of opposites facing each other. The Later Heaven sequence, attributed to King Wen, rotates the same trigrams into the directions used by feng shui and the calendar: fire south, water north, wood east, metal west, earth at the centre and the corners. The Earlier Heaven is cosmological, the Later Heaven is practical; most living traditions use the Later Heaven. The Shuogua commentary also maps them onto the body: heaven is the head, earth the belly, thunder the foot, wind the thigh, water the ear, fire the eye, mountain the hand, lake the mouth. Read from the outside in, it is a diagram of perception; read from the inside out, a diagram of the world. A trigram is a situation Not a substance and not a mood. Each one names a configuration of forces — thunder is movement breaking out of stillness, wind is what gets under a door, the lake is water resting in a hollow. When the Yijing speaks of a trigram it is describing the shape of a moment, not a thing in it. 易 易經 The sixty-four Two trigrams, one above the other, make a hexagram: eight times eight, sixty-four situations. The Yijing is the oldest book in the Chinese canon and the most commented on — a divination manual that became a cosmology. 易 yì means change, and also ease. The later tradition gives it three senses: the changing, the unchanging pattern in the change, and the simplicity of that pattern. The book itself is layered: a Bronze Age core of judgments and line texts, the Confucian commentaries called the Ten Wings ( 十翼 ), and two thousand years of further reading. How a hexagram is built Two trigrams — the lower three lines are the inner situation, the upper three the outer one. The book names a hexagram by the pair: “water over thunder” is 屯 . Six lines , read from the bottom ( 初 ) to the top ( 上 ). Yang lines are solid and numbered nine; yin lines are broken and numbered six. Positions 1, 3, 5 are yang places; 2, 4, 6 are yin places. A yang line in a yang place is "correct". Central lines — the second and the fifth — carry the most weight. The fifth is the ruler's seat. Correspondence pairs 1–4, 2–5 and 3–6: a line's relation to its partner matters as much as its position. Changing lines — marked old yang (9) or old yin (6) — flip into their opposite and produce a second, "resulting" hexagram. Nuclear hexagram — take lines 2–4 as a lower trigram and 3–5 as an upper one: the hidden situation inside the visible one. Reversed and inverted — 綜卦 turns the hexagram upside down, 錯卦 flips every line. The pair of opposites is often where the reading deepens. Two ways to cast The yarrow-stalk method is the classical one, described in the Xici : fifty stalks, one set aside, then three rounds of division and counting for each line. Its probabilities are uneven — old yin 1/16, young yang 5/16, young yin 7/16, old yang 3/16 — which gives the book a bias toward stability. The three-coin method is later and simpler: heads count 3, tails 2, the three coins give 6 to 9, and the four results are equally likely (1/8 each) — a flatter distribution than the yarrow stalks. The reading rules were only formalised late (Zhu Xi's scheme is the standard one): no changing lines, read the judgment; one, read that line; two, read the upper; three, read the nuclear hexagram; four, read the two unchanging lines; five, read the one unchanging line; six, read the extra judgment for a changing Qian or Kun. citizenHelper: Página Principal CitizenHelper Documentação técnica e institucional: um canal digital de apoio ao cidadão que aproxima a denúncia de crimes online do momento em que o crime acontece. Documento de apresentação para instituições públicas portuguesas. Versão 1.0 · Protótipo em fase de testes. 1. Resumo Grande parte da vida social dos portugueses decorre em redes como o Facebook e o Instagram. É aí que circulam ameaças, burlas, perseguições, vandalismo e conteúdos ilícitos, e é também aí que existem as provas: fotografias, vídeos e publicações com data e identificação. O CitizenHelper liga estes dois mundos: o cidadão indica a publicação, a localização e a descrição, e uma equipa institucional verificada consulta a denúncia numa lista atualizada em tempo real. A aplicação não substitui o 112, nem as queixas formais junto da PSP, GNR ou Polícia Judiciária. Funciona como um canal complementar, de baixa fricção, que pode encaminhar informação útil para as autoridades competentes. Em síntese: menos barreiras para denunciar, provas mais fáceis de identificar, acesso restrito a profissionais verificados e um registo técnico que pode ser auditado. 2. O problema Há três obstáculos recorrentes na denúncia de crimes praticados ou divulgados online: Fragmentação de canais. O cidadão tem de perceber qual o canal certo (112, Queixa Eletrónica, Polícia Judiciária, email, redes sociais das forças de segurança), cada um com regras próprias. Provas efémeras. Publicações podem ser apagadas, editadas ou tornadas privadas em minutos. Quanto mais tarde chega a denúncia, mais difícil é localizar o conteúdo. Barreira de formalidade. Uma queixa formal exige identificação e tempo. Muitas pessoas desistem antes de começar, sobretudo quando o incidente é recente ou ainda está a decorrer. 81,9% dos utilizadores de internet em Portugal usam redes sociais. DataReportal, outubro de 2025 (ver fontes). 24% dos inquiridos na UE afirmam já ter sido vítimas de fraude online. FRA, 2026. Dado europeu, não português. 15% das vítimas de fraude online na UE denunciaram à polícia. FRA, 2026. Mostra o fosso entre vitimização e denúncia. Os números europeus indicam que a maioria das vítimas de fraude online não chega às autoridades. Não é possível atribuir estes valores à população portuguesa, mas a tendência é suficientemente relevante para justificar um canal que reduza esse fosso. 3. Utilidade pública Para o cidadão Um único lugar para denunciar a partir do telemóvel, sem instalar nada. Partilha de localização e de uma ligação à publicação, sem necessidade de descarregar ou reenviar ficheiros. Contactos oficiais sempre à mão, incluindo o 112, a PSP, a GNR, a Polícia Judiciária, a APAV e linhas de apoio. Possibilidade de pedir uma videochamada com uma autoridade, quando a situação exige contacto direto. Para a sociedade Ponte entre a vida digital e a segurança física. A denúncia é feita onde o incidente aconteceu, sem obrigar o cidadão a trocar de contexto. Redução do tempo entre incidente e registo. A informação chega com data, localização e ligação à publicação, o que facilita a triagem. Encorajamento à denúncia. Quem hesita em fazer uma queixa formal pode começar por um formulário curto. Transparência do canal. Todos os passos e critérios de acesso estão documentados nesta página. Para as instituições Triagem mais rápida, com dados estruturados em vez de mensagens dispersas. Acesso restrito a emails institucionais verificados, o que reduz o risco de uso indevido. Registo auditável: cada denúncia tem código, data de criação e estado de tratamento. Complemento aos canais existentes, sem os substituir nem competir com eles. Nota de rigor. Uma denúncia na aplicação não tem, por si, valor de queixa criminal. Os crimes públicos e semipúblicos continuam a exigir os procedimentos legais próprios. A aplicação serve para registar e encaminhar informação. 4. Funcionamento O percurso típico de uma denúncia, do ponto de vista do cidadão: 1 Escolha o tipo de denúncia Mensagem de texto, ou foto/vídeo através da ligação da publicação no Facebook ou Instagram. 2 Descreva a situação Categoria (furto, violência, vandalismo, fraude online e outras), descrição e etiqueta opcional. A etiqueta #CitizenHelper é sempre acrescentada. 3 Partilhe a localização (opcional) O navegador pede autorização. A localização só é obtida no momento do envio, e o cidadão pode desativá-la. 4 Envie e guarde o código A denúncia recebe um código identificador, que o cidadão pode usar em contactos posteriores com as autoridades. 5 Pedir videochamada (opcional) Quando há urgência, o cidadão pede uma videochamada. Uma conta institucional verificada atende o pedido. Ligações de redes sociais: o que é aceite Por decisão de desenho, a aplicação não recebe ficheiros. Só aceita a ligação HTTPS de uma publicação do Facebook (incluindo fb.watch) ou do Instagram, e apenas para denúncias de foto ou vídeo. Esta regra é aplicada tanto no navegador como nas regras do servidor, o que evita dados que não sejam da rede social indicada. Porque não aceitar ficheiros? Armazenar fotografias e vídeos de terceiros levanta questões sérias de privacidade, de conservação e de direitos de imagem. Além disso, o ficheiro original continua na rede social, onde tem metadados e contexto. Ao registar a ligação, a aplicação aponta para a fonte sem duplicar conteúdo sensível. 5. Para as instituições O valor institucional do CitizenHelper depende de três garantias: quem acede, quando acede e o que fica registado. Quem acede Apenas contas com email verificado de domínio institucional ( psp.pt , pj.pt , gnr.pt , gov.pt e subdomínios). Emails pessoais, como Gmail ou Hotmail, são recusados no registo e no início de sessão. A verificação é feita em duas camadas: no navegador (para dar feedback imediato) e no servidor (funções de bloqueio do Firebase e regras de segurança), que é a camada que conta. Quando acede: tempo real As listas de pedidos de videochamada e, na fase seguinte, a lista de denúncias são subscrições em tempo real . O servidor envia cada alteração ao painel do profissional assim que é gravada, sem recarregar a página. Isto é tecnicamente feito com onSnapshot do Cloud Firestore. Estado atual: a subscrição em tempo real já está implementada para os pedidos de videochamada. O painel de triagem de denúncias ainda não existe; é o próximo passo do roteiro (secção 9). Arquitetura técnica A solução foi desenhada para ser simples de auditar e de manter. O frontend não tem etapa de compilação nem dependências locais: é um único ficheiro HTML com CSS e JavaScript, servido como página estática. Cliente (navegador) HTML5, CSS3 e JavaScript em módulos ES. Sem frameworks e sem bibliotecas externas além do SDK oficial do Firebase, carregado por ligação direta. Hospedagem GitHub Pages, com HTTPS obrigatório. As funções de geolocalização e de câmara exigem contexto seguro. Autenticação Firebase Authentication: email e palavra-passe para instituições, e sessão anónima para cidadãos que denunciam sem conta. Dados Cloud Firestore, com regras de segurança que definem quem lê e quem escreve, campo a campo. Lógica de servidor Funções de bloqueio (Identity Platform) que recusam contas não institucionais antes de qualquer sessão ser criada. Um site sem framework tem menos dependências a atualizar, menos superfície de ataque e um custo de manutenção baixo. Para um serviço público, a previsibilidade pesa mais do que a conveniência de ferramentas de desenvolvimento. O código fica legível por qualquer equipa técnica de uma entidade pública, sem formação específica. 7. Segurança e privacidade Mínimo de dados. Não são pedidos nome, morada nem número de telefone ao cidadão que denuncia. Sem ficheiros. Não há armazenamento de fotografias ou vídeos, o que reduz o risco de difusão indevida.
